note: NOT an engine run — the second trial of the chain-2 encoder (`astc-encoder.js` 1.0.0, ARM astcenc via wasm), taken to pick the two settings `createAstcEncoder` now DEFAULTS to: the quality preset and the thread count. Ran by Claude in the session container (x64 Linux, node 22, 4 cores) on a synthetic 256x256 RGBA8: two colour ramps plus a 16x16 checkerboard of BINARY alpha, so every block boundary meets a hard alpha edge — the shape SA's cutout foliage is made of and the one a block codec is worst at. Not comparable to the 08-06 trial (different image, different size, different thread count) and not comparable to anything else in this folder: no GPU, no pak, no device. What it establishes: MEDIUM is the KNEE — it buys +3.07 dB over FAST for 1.35x the time, while THOROUGH buys only another 0.30 dB for 1.41x again — and that astcenc's own worker pool is worth taking (threads=0 auto is 2.38x one thread on 4 cores, at bit-identical output). Both are why the encoder defaults to MEDIUM and threads=0. What this does NOT establish is the number chain 2 actually owes: the district A/B, two paks from one tree with only `--textures` flipped, which needs game assets this container does not have.
